label: Business / life coaching
summary: 12 weekly 1:1 sessions to set quarterly goals, fix the weekly operating rhythm and make the hire-or-not decision.
billing: 3-month package sold paid in full (about $1,250-$1,500) or as 3 monthly payments ($425-$500); client signs an agreement and completes intake before session 1. Sources: Paperbell package checkouts, Bonsai coaching fee guide.
ms: Done means the agreement is signed, the intake questionnaire is in and the 90-day goals are written and agreed in session 1.
Done means sessions 2-4 are held and a weekly scorecard is in use for two straight weeks.
Done means sessions 5-8 are held and the hiring decision has a written yes or no with a date.
Done means sessions 9-12 are held and the client has a written 90-day review and a next-quarter plan.
waiting: Between-session homework: the weekly scorecard or worksheet before the next call.
ask: How do you want to continue after the 90 days?
Renewal pricing is held if decided before session 12.
checkin: - Done: session 6 held, delegation list finished
- Next: draft the hiring scorecard together on Tuesday
- Needs from you: this week's scorecard numbers by Monday night
talk: Quick nudge: send this week's scorecard before Tuesday so we can spend the call on the hire decision.
Will do. Revenue was down but I hit 4 of 5 habits.
Good, that's the conversation. Bring the two candidate names too.
anxieties: Am I actually making progress or just talking?
What did we agree last session and what is my homework?
When do my payments run and how many sessions are left?
notes: Highly variable content but a fixed shape (N sessions over M months). Portal should show sessions used vs remaining, homework due, session notes shared by the coach, payment-plan schedule. Coaching is not therapy; if the business is a licensed therapist or counselor it needs PHI handling and is out of scope.

label: Fitness or nutrition coaching program
summary: Custom training block plus macro targets with weekly check-ins and a re-plan every 4 weeks.
billing: Monthly subscription for online coaching (commonly $150-$300/mo) or a 12-week program paid up front; in-person trainers sell session packs (10 or 20 sessions) paid in advance. Sources: Practice Better and Trainerize program docs.
ms: Done means intake, goals, starting photos and measurements are in and the first 4-week block is delivered in the app.
Done means 4 weekly check-ins are submitted and reviewed and macros are adjusted once.
Done means the progress review is held and block 2 lifts and targets are updated from block 1 results.
Done means final photos and measurements are compared against day 1 and a maintenance or next-phase plan is delivered.
waiting: The weekly check-in form (weight trend, photos, adherence, how training felt).
ask: Decide by week 11 so block 4 is ready.
checkin: - Done: week 6 check-in reviewed, calories lowered by 150
- Next: block 2 deload in week 8
- Needs from you: Sunday check-in with front and side photos
talk: Your week 6 numbers look good. I dropped carbs slightly; new targets are in the app.
Thanks. Bench stalled at 185 though.
Expected on a cut. We hold it and push reps; that's in block 2.
anxieties: Am I on track or is the scale lying?
Did my coach see my check-in and what changed?
What am I supposed to eat and lift this week?
notes: Recurring weekly loop more than a one-off job. Progress photos are sensitive and must be private to client and coach. If a registered dietitian handles medical nutrition therapy, that is PHI (HIPAA) and out of scope; general fitness coaching is fine.

label: Tutoring / test prep
summary: Diagnostic, 20 hours of 1:1 tutoring and 4 full-length practice tests aimed at the March SAT.
billing: Hour packages paid up front (e.g. 16 hours about $1,029, 24 hours about $1,449; typical 20-40 hour program $900-$3,200), starting from a full-length diagnostic. Sources: Leland SAT packages, IvyStrides 2026 pricing guide, PrepScholar.
ms: Done means a full-length diagnostic is scored and a study plan with a target score and test date is shared with the parent.
Done means 8 sessions are held and practice test 1 shows the weakest section improving.
Done means 8 more sessions are held and practice tests 2 and 3 are taken under timed conditions.
Done means the last practice test is reviewed, test-day plan is set and the official score is recorded after the test.
waiting: The student finishing the timed practice test and homework before the next session.
ask: Which test date should we target?
A second sitting usually needs 6 more hours.
checkin: - Done: practice test 2 scored 1340 (+90 from diagnostic)
- Next: reading pacing drills in sessions 11-12
- Needs from you: Arjun to take practice test 3 this Saturday, timed
talk: Practice test 2 came in at 1340, up 90. Math is strong; reading timing is the gap.
Great. Should he do extra reading at home?
Yes, two timed passages a night. I'll send the set.
anxieties: Is the score actually going up?
How many hours are left in the package?
Is the student doing the homework and showing up?
notes: Client is usually a parent paying for a minor; portal needs parent and student views and must not expose more student data than needed (FERPA applies to schools, not private tutors, but privacy still matters). Hours used vs remaining and score trend are the core status.

label: College admissions consulting
summary: College list, Common App personal statement, supplements for 10 schools and a deadline tracker through Regular Decision.
billing: Flat comprehensive package (most families about $6,500; junior/senior packages $5,000 and up), usually a deposit at signing and the balance in installments; essay-only packages $1,500+. Sources: Private Prep 2026 cost report, Paperbell senior package, Varsity Tutors.
ms: Done means a balanced list (reach, target, likely) of 10 schools is agreed by student and parents with ED/EA choices decided.
Done means the Common App essay is through up to 4 drafts and the student marks it final.
Done means every supplement for all 10 schools is final and the activities list and honors are entered.
Done means each application is submitted by its deadline and confirmation pages are saved.
waiting: The student's next essay draft by the agreed date.
ask: Apply Early Decision to which school?
ED is binding; we discuss aid first.
checkin: - Done: personal statement final, 6 of 14 supplements final
- Next: Boston College and Tufts supplements
- Needs from you: Sofia's Tufts draft by Friday; parents confirm the ED choice
talk: The personal statement is final. Sofia's Tufts supplement is next; can she get me a draft by Friday?
She has a soccer tournament, can it be Sunday?
Sunday works. That keeps us on track for November 1.
anxieties: Are we going to make the November 1 deadline?
Which essays are done and which are left?
Is the list too reachy?
notes: Deadline-driven with many parallel items (one per school). Portal should show a per-school tracker and essay draft count; parents and student are separate viewers. Student data privacy matters; no PHI unless disability accommodations are discussed (keep out).

label: Auto repair (mechanical)
project: 2017 Honda Accord: Check Engine Light and Brakes
summary: Diagnose the check engine light, replace front pads and rotors, and inspect the rest of the car.
billing: Diagnostic fee up front (often credited to the repair), then a repair order estimate the customer approves by text; paid in full at pickup. Sources: Tekmetric digital authorization and DVI guides.
ms: Done means the code is read, the cause is confirmed and a digital inspection with photos is sent.
Done means the customer has approved or declined each line on the estimate by digital signature.
Done means approved work is done and the car passes a road test with no light.
Done means the invoice is paid and the keys are handed over with notes on deferred work.
waiting: Approval of the estimate (the car sits on the lift until they answer).
ask: Rear brakes are at 3mm. Do them now?
checkin: - Done: diagnosed, purge valve failed, front brakes at 2mm
- Next: install once you approve
- Needs from you: approve or decline each line on the estimate
talk: Inspection is in your texts with photos. Purge valve is the light; front brakes are metal-close. Approve what you want and we start.
Do the brakes and the valve. Skip the cabin filter.
Done, parts are here at 2. Ready by 5.
anxieties: How much is this going to cost and is it all necessary?
When will my car be ready?
Did you find anything else?
notes: Approval of an estimate with line-by-line accept/decline and photos/videos is the central portal action. Parts on order and waiting-on-customer are distinct statuses. Signed authorization records matter legally in many states.

label: Auto body / collision repair
summary: Insurance-paid repair of the rear bumper, liftgate and sensors, including a supplement for hidden damage.
billing: Insurer pays the approved estimate plus supplements directly to the shop; customer pays the deductible at pickup. Sources: Central Insurance and ER Lawyers on supplements, BodyShop Business.
ms: Done means the shop estimate is written and the insurer has the claim number, photos and estimate.
Done means hidden damage found at teardown is documented and the insurer approves the supplement.
Done means structural and body work is done, paint is matched and the rear sensors are calibrated.
Done means quality check, wash and delivery are done and the deductible is paid.
waiting: Sign-off on the repair authorization and the deductible; often the insurer, not the client, is the bottleneck.
ask: The liftgate is on backorder 2 weeks. What do you want to do?
Aftermarket may need your insurer's okay.
answered: Through the insurer, Enterprise, until delivery
checkin: - Done: teardown, supplement for the bumper reinforcement approved
- Next: paint once the liftgate arrives
- Needs from you: decide OEM vs aftermarket liftgate
talk: Supplement approved. The OEM liftgate is backordered until the 14th.
Ugh. Does my rental cover that long?
We asked your adjuster to extend it; I'll confirm today.
anxieties: When will my car be done?
Is insurance paying for this and what do I owe?
Will the paint match and is it safe?
notes: Third party (insurer/adjuster) drives approvals; portal needs an insurance status line separate from client tasks. Parts backorders cause most delays. Many photos.

label: Custom manufacturing / fabrication
summary: Design, fabricate and install a stainless work platform with railings for a brewery cellar.
billing: Quote tied to a drawing revision; deposit at acceptance (often 30-50%), progress payment at shop-drawing approval or mid-fabrication, balance on delivery/install; change orders billed separately. Sources: WOODWEB payment schedule thread, InvoiceQuick fabrication invoice guide.
ms: Done means the quote referencing drawing rev A is signed and the deposit is received.
Done means the client signs off the shop drawings; changes after this are change orders.
Done means all parts are cut, welded and finished and pass the in-shop inspection with photos.
Done means the platform is installed, anchored and walked by the client.
waiting: Signed approval of the shop drawings (fabrication cannot start until then).
ask: Cable adds a week and about $1,800.
checkin: - Done: material arrived, deck frame welded
- Next: railings and stair stringers
- Needs from you: confirm the install date and that the floor is clear
talk: Frame is welded, photos attached. We can install the 18th if the floor is clear.
18th works but the tank delivery is the 17th.
Then we'll come the 19th. Locking it in.
anxieties: Is it on schedule?
Will it fit and match what we approved?
What will change orders cost?
notes: Every job is unique; drawings and revisions must be versioned and tied to approvals. Change orders and progress billing are core. Photos of work in progress reduce anxiety.

label: Screen printing / custom apparel order
summary: 250 tri-blend tees, 2-color front print, sizes S-3XL, delivered a week before race day.
billing: Quote approved, then deposit (commonly 50%) before ordering blanks; mockup/proof must be approved before production; balance due on pickup or delivery. Sources: Printavo approvals docs and status-message templates.
ms: Done means quantities, garment and price are approved and the deposit is paid.
Done means the client approves the final mockup with print size, placement and ink colors.
Done means blanks arrived, screens burned and all 250 printed and counted by size.
Done means the balance is paid and the order is picked up or delivered.
waiting: Mockup approval and the final size breakdown.
ask: Ink color on the heather grey tee?
White underbase not needed for navy.
checkin: - Done: deposit in, blanks ordered
- Next: print Thursday once mockup is approved
- Needs from you: approve the mockup and final sizes by Tuesday
talk: Mockup is attached. Approve it and send final sizes by Tuesday to make Thursday's press.
Logo looks small, can it be bigger?
Bumped to 11 inches wide; new mockup sent.
anxieties: Will it be ready before the event?
Will the colors and size look like the mockup?
Are the size counts right?
notes: Two separate approvals (quote and artwork) plus a size breakdown; Printavo now handles quote and art approvals separately. Hard deadlines tied to events. Blanks out of stock is a common delay.

label: Custom jewelry
project: Custom Oval Engagement Ring, Hidden Halo
summary: 1.5 ct oval lab diamond in a platinum hidden-halo setting, ready before a June proposal.
billing: 50% deposit (often non-refundable) to start stone sourcing and CAD, balance on completion; some take a small fixed deposit and invoice after the client approves finished-piece photos. 4-10 weeks. Sources: Revolution Jewelry Works, I Hate Steven Singer, 25 Karats.
ms: Done means style, budget and stone spec are agreed and the 50% deposit is paid.
Done means the client approves the CAD renders (up to 3 revisions included).
Done means the piece is cast in platinum, the stone is set and finished.
Done means the client approves final photos, pays the balance and picks up with the appraisal.
waiting: Approval of the CAD render (changes are cheap before casting and impossible after).
ask: Thinner looks daintier; 2.0 is the most common.
checkin: - Done: stone in hand, CAD v2 sent
- Next: cast once CAD is approved
- Needs from you: approve CAD v2 or send changes
talk: CAD v2 is attached with the thinner band you asked for. Once you approve, we cast.
Can the halo sit a bit lower?
Yes, 0.3 mm lower in v3 tomorrow. Still on track for May 20.
anxieties: Will it be ready before the proposal date?
Will it look like the render?
Is the stone the one I picked and is it real?
notes: High-trust, secrecy matters (surprise proposals: don't message a partner). Render images and stone certificates must be viewable. Approval gate before casting is critical.

label: Tailoring / bridal alterations
summary: Take in bodice, hem with shoes, add a French bustle; 3 fittings starting 10 weeks out.
billing: Price set at the first fitting after seeing the gown; payment or a deposit (one shop: 60%) at first fitting, balance at pickup; typical $500-$1,000; rush fee inside 3 weeks. Sources: David's Bridal alterations FAQ, The Knot, myneworleans.com.
ms: Done means the gown is pinned, work list and price are agreed and the deposit is paid.
Done means bodice and hem are checked on the client and any tweaks are marked.
Done means the client approves the fit and the bustle is demonstrated to whoever will do it on the day.
Done means balance is paid and the gown is picked up pressed.
waiting: Bringing the wedding shoes and undergarments to the fitting, and booking the next fitting.
checkin: - Done: first fitting, bodice taken in 1 inch
- Next: second fitting May 10
- Needs from you: bring the actual shoes and your bustle helper to the final
talk: Bodice is done. Bring your shoes on the 10th so we lock the hem.
Shoes haven't arrived yet!
Bring heels the same height and we'll check again at the final.
anxieties: Will it be ready in time for the wedding?
Will it fit if my weight changes?
What does it cost in total?
notes: Appointment-driven milestones with a hard date. Price is only known after first fitting. Pickup and payment are tied. Photos of the client in the gown are sensitive and private.

label: Travel planning (custom trip)
summary: Rome, Amalfi Coast and Florence with hotels, trains, a cooking class and private transfers.
billing: Non-refundable planning fee or retainer (e.g. $100-$400, credited or not) before itinerary work; trip costs paid to suppliers on their deposit and final-payment schedule (final often 45-90 days before travel). Travefy collects planning fees only, not bookings. Sources: Travefy planning fee docs, Expedia advisor-curated trips.
ms: Done means the trip brief (dates, budget, style) is agreed and the planning fee is paid.
Done means the client approves the day-by-day proposal and hotel choices.
Done means hotels, trains and tours are booked with deposits paid and confirmations attached.
Done means final payments are made and the mobile itinerary with all confirmations is shared.
waiting: Approval of the itinerary proposal, then names-as-on-passport and card authorization for deposits.
ask: Positano is liveliest; Ravello is quietest.
answered: Yes, comprehensive, quoted with the booking
checkin: - Done: Rome and Florence hotels booked
- Next: Amalfi hotel once you pick a town
- Needs from you: choose the Amalfi base and sign the card authorization
talk: Rome and Florence are confirmed. Pick your Amalfi base and I'll hold the room today.
Positano! Is the sea-view upgrade worth it?
For a honeymoon, yes. It's 140 euros a night more. Holding both.
anxieties: Is everything actually booked and confirmed?
When are payments due and how much?
What happens if a flight or plan changes?
notes: Many suppliers each with their own deposit and final-payment dates; the advisor usually does not collect trip money themselves. Portal must show confirmations and a payment calendar; passport and card data must never sit in plain text.

label: Pet training program
summary: Six in-home lessons for a 7-month lab: loose-leash walking, place, recall and door manners.
billing: Prepaid package (6-week basic about $400 for six sessions; in-home packages to $1,300); board-and-train 6 weeks about $2,500-$3,800 with a deposit and follow-up lessons. Sources: Cottonball Canines, Leader of the Pack, All 4 Paws.
ms: Done means the dog is evaluated, goals are set and the package is paid.
Done means sit, down, place and name response work at home with mild distraction.
Done means loose-leash walk and recall work on a neighborhood walk.
Done means the dog performs all goals in public and the owner has a maintenance plan.
waiting: Daily practice at home and the practice log or short videos between lessons.
checkin: - Done: lesson 3, place is solid
- Next: loose-leash walk on your street
- Needs from you: two 5-minute sessions a day and a video of a walk
talk: Biscuit nailed place today. Send me a 30-second walk video before Thursday.
He pulls like crazy when he sees squirrels.
Normal. We'll work distance from squirrels Thursday.
anxieties: Is my dog actually improving?
Am I doing the homework right?
What do I do when he reacts or regresses?
notes: Outcomes depend on owner homework, so homework and videos are the core of the portal. Vaccine records are required but not PHI. Board-and-train adds daily updates and photos.

label: Translation services
project: Spanish to English: Contracts Bundle, 18,000 Words
summary: Translate and certify 6 contracts for a court filing, with a client glossary and one review round.
billing: Per source word ($0.07-$0.11 legal), certified work per page ($20-$25 per 200-250 word page) plus notarization; rush surcharge; often full prepayment for new clients or 50% on large projects. Sources: Polilingua rate guide, BeTranslated rates, Translayte.
ms: Done means final source files are received, word count quoted and the quote accepted with payment.
Done means key legal terms and party names are agreed with the client before translation.
Done means all files are translated and independently edited (TEP).
Done means client review is done and signed certificates are delivered.
waiting: Final source files (not drafts) and confirmation of the glossary terms.
ask: Notarization adds $25 per document and a day.
checkin: - Done: 4 of 6 contracts translated
- Next: editing pass and the last 2 files
- Needs from you: confirm the spelling of the two company names
talk: Four contracts are translated. Can you confirm the exact English names of the two companies?
Use the names from the Delaware filing, I'll send it.
Perfect, that locks the glossary. Delivery Thursday.
anxieties: Will it be ready for my deadline?
Will the court or agency accept the certification?
Are my documents confidential?
notes: Confidential documents (immigration, legal); medical records translation can involve PHI and should be excluded or handled under a BAA. Portal needs secure file upload and delivery and a per-file status.

label: IT services / managed IT onboarding
summary: Take over IT for a 22-person office: discovery, admin access, security baseline and help desk go-live in 30 days.
billing: One-time onboarding fee scoped at signing (often one month's fee), then per-user or per-device monthly agreement. Sources: NuOptima MSP onboarding checklist, Datapath 30-60-90 plan.
ms: Done means the agreement is signed, contacts named and admin credentials handed over from the old provider.
Done means every device, license and account is inventoried and documented.
Done means MFA, patching, endpoint protection and working backups are in place.
Done means users have the support process and the 30-day review is held with a roadmap.
waiting: Credentials and access from the outgoing IT provider, and a list of users with roles.
ask: Old file server: move to cloud or replace?
checkin: - Done: agents on 20 of 22 PCs, backups fixed
- Next: roll out MFA Monday
- Needs from you: tell staff about MFA and the 2 laptops still offsite
talk: Backups were failing for 3 weeks; fixed and tested. MFA rolls out Monday.
Glad you caught it. Will people get locked out?
No, we'll be on site 8-10 to enroll everyone.
anxieties: Is my data safe during the switch?
Will this disrupt work?
Who do my staff call now?
notes: Credentials are shared during onboarding; portal must never store passwords in plain text (link to a vault). If the client is a medical practice, the MSP may need a BAA; keep PHI out of the portal.

label: 3D printing / prototyping
summary: Three rounds of SLA-printed enclosures for a handheld sensor, with DFM feedback each round.
billing: Instant or manual quote from uploaded STL/STEP; most online services charge at order before printing; small shops quote per part and often take payment up front or net-30 for business clients. Lead times 1-6 business days by process. Sources: Hubs, Fictiv, 3DPrintingServices.
ms: Done means STEP files pass the DFM check and the quote for 3 iterations is approved.
Done means rev 1 parts are printed, post-processed and fit-checked by the client.
Done means rev 2 incorporates feedback and the snap fit works.
Done means rev 3 is printed, painted and approved as the looks-like/works-like prototype.
waiting: Updated CAD files after each fit check.
checkin: - Done: rev 1 shipped, snap clip cracked
- Next: rev 2 with thicker clip
- Needs from you: updated STEP file with 1.5 mm clip
talk: Rev 1 clips cracked at 1 mm. I'd go 1.5 mm in tough resin.
Makes sense. File coming tonight.
Got it, prints tomorrow, ships Friday.
anxieties: Will it work this time?
How fast can I get it?
Is my design confidential (NDA)?
notes: Iterative jobs with file versions per round; portal needs file upload/versioning and NDA-friendly privacy. Overlaps with custom fabrication; could merge as a sub-template.

label: Event rentals
project: Backyard Wedding: Tent, 120 Chairs, Tables and Lighting
summary: 40x60 tent, 120 chairs, 15 rounds, linens and bistro lights delivered, set up and picked up.
billing: 50% deposit when the quote is accepted (often non-refundable), balance 7-14 days before delivery; damage waiver around 10% of subtotal; delivery/setup fee by distance and site. Sources: Bella Acento and Carried Away (TapGoods) FAQs, Regina Special Event Rentals policies.
ms: Done means the item list and date are confirmed and the 50% deposit is paid.
Done means final quantities and the layout are locked (often 2-6 weeks out).
Done means the balance is paid and everything is delivered and set up.
Done means items are picked up, counted and any damage is settled.
waiting: Final headcount and layout, and confirming site access for the tent.
ask: Add sidewalls in case of rain?
checkin: - Done: contract and deposit
- Next: utility locate before staking the tent
- Needs from you: final headcount and layout by May 1
talk: Need your final headcount and layout by May 1 so we can load the truck.
We're at 112 but a few maybes.
Book for 120; you can drop to 112 up to 7 days out.
anxieties: Will everything arrive on time and set up correctly?
What if it rains?
What am I charged for damage?
notes: Inventory-based rather than custom work, so jobs are similar; a single hard date. Portal needs item list edits up to a cutoff, payment schedule and delivery window.
